title: A multifunctional magnetic composite Fe 3 O 4 @MOF-919 for dual-function bacterial clearance and IL-6 removal in hemoperfusion
content: Magnetic materials derived from metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have garnered considerable interest as adsorbents for hemoperfusion. Herein, a novel magnetic metal–organic framework composite adsorbent, Fe3O4@MOF-919, was designed and synthesized to address the clinical challenge of dual-functionally removing drug-resistant pathogens and inflammatory mediators in bloodstream infections (BSI). Under identical experimental conditions, Fe3O4@MOF-919 exhibited exceptional antibacterial efficacy, achieving removal efficiencies of 99.4% against CREO, 99.8% against CRKP, and 99.6% against MRSA. These results are attributable to the synergistic coordination between bacterial surface moieties and the Cu2+/Fe3+ sites and carboxylate ligands of the MOF-919(Fe–Cu) shell. Simultaneously, the composite demonstrated a high adsorption efficiency for IL-6 in simulated serum (96.68% within 3 h, equivalent to 70.58 ng g−1), following a physical adsorption mechanism. Crucially, Fe3O4@MOF-919 also shows a hemolysis rate below 5%, negligible impact on coagulation function and blood cells, and Grade 1 cytotoxicity. By physically removing pathogens and cytokines without inducing drug resistance, Fe3O4@MOF-919 provides a safe and effective adsorbent platform for drug-resistant BSI and sepsis, demonstrating considerable potential for future biomedical applications.
